words.definition: a molecule made of two hydrogen atoms covalently bonded to one oxygen atom
words.example: A water molecule has an uneven distribution of charge because oxygen attracts electrons more strongly than hydrogen.

words.definition: a covalent bond in which electrons are shared unequally between atoms
words.example: The O–H bonds in water are polar covalent bonds.

words.definition: an unequal distribution of electrical charge within a molecule
words.example: The polarity of water allows it to interact strongly with ions and other polar molecules.

words.definition: a small positive or negative charge caused by unequal sharing of electrons in a covalent bond
words.example: Oxygen carries a partial negative charge in a water molecule.

words.definition: a weak attraction between a partially positive hydrogen atom and an electronegative atom in another molecule or region
words.example: Hydrogen bonds between water molecules contribute to cohesion.

words.definition: attraction between molecules of the same substance
words.example: Cohesion between water molecules helps maintain continuous water columns in plant xylem.

words.definition: the tendency of a liquid surface to resist stretching because of cohesive forces
words.example: Water has high surface tension because surface molecules are held together by hydrogen bonds.

words.definition: a substance that dissolves another substance to form a solution
words.example: Water acts as a solvent for many ions and polar molecules in cells.

words.definition: a substance dissolved in a solvent
words.example: Glucose can act as a solute when dissolved in water.

words.definition: a solution in which water is the solvent
words.example: Cytoplasm contains many substances in aqueous solution.

words.definition: having an affinity for water and tending to interact with or dissolve in it
words.example: Ions and polar molecules are generally hydrophilic.

words.definition: repelled by water and tending not to dissolve in it
words.example: Hydrophobic fatty-acid tails cluster away from water in membranes.

words.definition: the energy required to raise the temperature of a unit mass of a substance by one degree
words.example: Water has a high specific heat capacity, which helps stabilize body and habitat temperatures.

words.definition: the ability of a substance to transfer heat through direct contact
words.example: Water transfers heat effectively because of its relatively high thermal conductivity.

words.definition: the upward force exerted by a fluid that supports an immersed object
words.example: Buoyancy reduces the need for heavy support structures in many aquatic organisms.

words.definition: a measure of a fluid's resistance to flow
words.example: Water's viscosity affects how small organisms move through aquatic environments.

words.definition: deoxyribonucleic acid, the double-stranded molecule that stores hereditary information in cells
words.example: DNA stores the base sequence that can be inherited and used to make RNA.

words.definition: ribonucleic acid, usually a single-stranded nucleic acid involved in gene expression
words.example: Messenger RNA carries genetic information from DNA to ribosomes.

words.definition: the monomer of nucleic acids, consisting of a phosphate group, a pentose sugar and a nitrogenous base
words.example: DNA and RNA are polymers built from nucleotide monomers.

words.definition: a phosphorus-containing group that forms part of the backbone of nucleic acids
words.example: Phosphate groups link sugars together in the DNA backbone.

words.definition: a sugar containing five carbon atoms
words.example: Deoxyribose and ribose are pentose sugars found in nucleic acids.

words.definition: a nitrogen-containing component of a nucleotide that can form specific base pairs
words.example: The sequence of nitrogenous bases carries genetic information.

words.definition: the alternating chain of pentose sugars and phosphate groups forming the structural framework of a nucleic-acid strand
words.example: The bases project inward from the sugar-phosphate backbone of DNA.

words.definition: a purine base present in DNA and RNA that pairs with thymine in DNA and uracil in RNA
words.example: Adenine forms complementary base pairs with thymine in DNA.

words.definition: a pyrimidine base found in DNA that pairs with adenine
words.example: Thymine is present in DNA but not normally in RNA.

words.definition: a pyrimidine base found in DNA and RNA that pairs with guanine
words.example: Cytosine forms three hydrogen bonds with guanine in DNA.

words.definition: a purine base found in DNA and RNA that pairs with cytosine
words.example: Guanine pairs specifically with cytosine.

words.definition: a pyrimidine base found in RNA that pairs with adenine
words.example: Uracil replaces thymine as the complementary base to adenine in RNA.

words.definition: the structure formed by two DNA strands twisted around each other
words.example: The DNA double helix is stabilized by base pairing between the two strands.

words.definition: two nucleic-acid strands that run in opposite 5′ to 3′ directions
words.example: The two strands of DNA are antiparallel.

words.definition: specific pairing of nitrogenous bases according to chemical compatibility
words.example: Complementary base pairing allows an accurate copy of DNA to be made.

words.definition: the order of nitrogenous bases along a DNA or RNA strand
words.example: Changes in a DNA base sequence can create mutations.

words.definition: the set of rules by which nucleotide triplets in mRNA specify amino acids or stop signals
words.example: The genetic code links mRNA codons to amino acids during translation.
